[medium] This introduces a subtle behavior change: `serialize()` falls back to its default truncation limits (MAX_TEXT_LENGTH=20000, MAX_ITEMS_LENGTH=1000), whereas the old `serialize_field()` never truncated. Vertex build `data` and `artifacts` persisted to the DB/logs could therefore be cut off without warning. If full fidelity matters for debugging/auditing, pass `max_length=None, max_items=None` here, or use a dedicated `serialize_or_str`/configurable limits instead.

```suggestion
            data=serialize(data, max_length=None, max_items=None),
            # Serialize artifacts using our custom serializer
            artifacts=serialize(artifacts, max_length=None, max_items=None) if artifacts else None,
```

[medium] The specific object-type arms on lines 161-165 (Enum, TypeVar, and Type alias/generic types) can never execute, because they sit after the generic `case object() if not isinstance(obj, type):` on line 159. Python evaluates match cases in order and takes the first match, and line 159 already matches any instance that isn't a class — so Enums, TypeVars, and Type aliases all get captured before reaching their dedicated handlers.

Suggestion: reorder so the specific object type cases (Enum, TypeVar, Type alias) come before the generic object() instance case.
[low] The `_serialize_str` behavior could use a test that confirms the result remains deterministic.
[low] The lifecycle of `Pinecone` could be clearer if this code documented who owns its updates.
